summary: Heir to an oil fortune, Stockton Rush founded OceanGate in 2009 and sold seats on Titan, a carbon-fibre submersible built against expert safety warnings, until it imploded on a 2023 dive to the Titanic wreck, killing all five aboard.

evidence.note: Post-recording insert gives birth as 1962 in San Francisco per obituaries
OceanGate founded in 2009; part one ends here
Family wealth from Standard Oil and Indonesian oil, Bohemian Club ties
Titanic wreck discovery and Titanic tourism history as context for his business
Rejects titanium norms for a carbon-fibre pressure hull, dismisses expert warnings
Long comparison to tech-industry disruption culture and tech bros
Marine operations director raises hull and viewport concerns, is fired and sued
Open letter from about forty industry figures warns the craft is unsafe
OceanGate promo video and uncritical press coverage analysed at length
Moves to Seattle area; cold-water diving there leads to submersibles
Support vessel registered in Canada, dives in international waters

notes: Released days after the 2023 implosion but told as a biography, so deep-dive. A segment on slaveholding ancestors Richard Stockton and Benjamin Rush (about 8 min) is family background, kept out of subjects, themes and covered years. The wreck lies in international waters; CA added as the nearest country and registry. OceanGate treated as non-tech, hence business-executive over tech-founder.
